_comment: Context layer vector store on OpenSearch (self-managed, Amazon OpenSearch Service, or OpenSearch Serverless vector collections), implementing schemas/vector/metadata-contract.md. 'index_body' is the body of PUT /context-chunks (strip the _comment keys and the example_* sections first). k-NN with HNSW and cosine similarity to match the other stores in this folder. Fictional tenants only (Globex Logistics is CLIENT-001).
isolation_note: Three layers, use at least two. (1) Every query carries a bool filter on tenant_id, visibility and status, built by the retrieval service from the caller's identity (rule 1). (2) A filtered alias per tenant (example below) so a tenant's client can only address an alias that already carries its tenant filter. (3) With the Security plugin, document-level security on the reader role (DLS query {"term": {"tenant_id": "CLIENT-001"}}) enforces the boundary inside the cluster regardless of what the query says; for a regulated client, use one index per tenant. Audience is decided per index: an index client users can query holds only client_shared and public chunks.

mapping_notes._comment: Why each field is mapped as it is.
mapping_notes.dynamic strict: A chunk with an unexpected field is rejected instead of silently adding a mapping; the metadata contract is the whole set of fields.
mapping_notes.id: Also used as the document _id (deterministic {source_system}:{source_id}#{chunk_index}) so indexing is an upsert; kept as a keyword field too because _id cannot be aggregated.
mapping_notes.tenant_id, status, visibility: keyword so term filters are exact and cheap; these three are on every query.
mapping_notes.source_url: Stored and returned but not indexed; it is the citation, nobody searches it.
mapping_notes.text: Analyzed text for hybrid (BM25 + k-NN) retrieval; returned with the match.
mapping_notes.embedding: knn_vector, 1536 dimensions, HNSW, cosinesimil. The lucene engine supports efficient (pre-)filtering, which is what makes the filtered query below return a full k. faiss also supports efficient filtering; nmslib does not and would post-filter. Changing dimensions means a new index and a full re-embed.
mapping_notes.generated_at, last_synced_at: date fields; max(last_synced_at) per tenant_id is the freshness heartbeat (aggregation below).
mapping_notes.metadata: object with enabled false: stored verbatim, never indexed, so extras (heading_path, title) cannot collide with the strict mapping. Never secrets, never personal data.

example_document._comment: PUT /context-chunks/_doc/notion:p-readme#0 (URL-encode the id). The vector is truncated here.
example_document.text: Client README > Who we are. Globex Logistics engagement readme, chunk 0 ...

example_query_bool_filter._comment: POST /context-chunks/_search. The classic shape: k-NN in must, the three governance filters in filter. Note that with this shape the k-NN clause returns its k nearest per shard first and the filter is applied afterwards, so fewer than k rows can come back when a tenant is small; prefer example_query_efficient_filter when the engine supports it. _source names the citation fields.

example_query_efficient_filter._comment: Same governance filter placed inside the knn clause. With the lucene or faiss engine the filter is applied during the HNSW search, so all k results satisfy tenant_id AND visibility AND status. This is the recommended shape.

example_tenant_alias._comment: POST /_aliases. A filtered alias per tenant; the tenant's retrieval client is given only the alias name, never the index name. The query filter is still required (rule 1).

example_delete_source._comment: POST /context-chunks/_delete_by_query. Removing a deprecated or changed page before indexing its new chunks, so a query never sees old and new together.

example_freshness_aggregation._comment: POST /context-chunks/_search. The heartbeat per tenant; compare with the contract's freshness.stale_after_days before the first query of a run.
